entry.title: [HIGH] claude-security scan-changes can analyze the wrong diff content.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.259 Windows claude-security `scan-changes` run recorded the intended merge-base and head commit in `scan-meta.json`, but its inventory and research output repeatedly analyzed unrelated CI workflow files from outside the requested range. A retry with a fresh report directory and workflow run id reproduced the same wrong result, while a plain `git diff --numstat <merge-base>..<HEAD>` showed the actual range touched application and test files instead. Security-review output can therefore look tied to the correct revision pair while its conclusions, hot-file list, and component-change claims come from different content.

entry.title: [HIGH] Cowork network allowlists can ignore user sandbox settings.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.260 macOS Cowork setup found that changing `sandbox.enabled` and `sandbox.network.allowedDomains` in `~/.claude/settings.json` did not affect egress from the Cowork Linux sandbox. The same curl probe kept allowing only platform-default domains such as `registry.npmjs.org` while blocking user-added domains with a proxy `blocked-by-allowlist` response, and setting `sandbox.enabled: false` did not lift the Cowork restriction. The reporter observed an in-sandbox proxy and root-owned `/etc/srt-settings.base.json` policy that appeared separate from the user's Claude settings, so local CLI sandbox configuration can look authoritative while Cowork uses a fixed remote/platform allowlist.

entry.title: [HIGH] CLI plugin uninstall can leave orphaned background security hooks.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.209 Windows setup found that uninstalling the official `security-guidance` plugin from the CLI could leave an already queued background review hook pointing at a deleted session-local plugin directory. Subsequent unrelated sessions kept showing repeated background security-review notifications with a missing `security_reminder_hook.py` path, and the reporter later saw the desktop app become unresponsive with many Claude processes until forced closed. The narrower risk is that CLI uninstall and the in-app plugin registry can diverge, so a removed plugin may still drive cross-session notification and hook state.

entry.title: [MEDIUM] `--setting-sources` docs can hide what hooks, plugins, and memory are isolated.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.261 Windows headless repro found that the CLI docs' short `--setting-sources user,project,local` description does not explain the actual isolation boundary. Omitting `user` reportedly drops `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, user settings, plugins, plugin hooks, user skills, agents, and commands, while project `CLAUDE.md`, project settings, project hooks, `.mcp.json`, auto-memory, project commands, and an explicit `--settings` file can still load. A related macOS report found that `--setting-sources project` could still load user `CLAUDE.md` and rules when the project path sits under `$HOME`, and an older feature request shows users already expected source filtering to cover more than `settings.json`. Headless jobs that use the flag for clean repo-owned execution can therefore either lose expected user/plugin guardrails or inherit user memory in path-dependent ways without documentation making the boundary obvious.

entry.title: [HIGH] Bash-first file access can skip nested CLAUDE.md context.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.260 macOS repro found that sessions in bypassPermissions or auto mode can receive an internal Bash-first instruction that steers routine reads through `cat`, `head`, or `sed -n` instead of the dedicated Read tool. In the repro, reading `src/sub/hello.txt` through Read loaded both the matching path-scoped rule and `src/sub/CLAUDE.md`, but reading the same file with Bash returned the file content without the nested context tokens. The same report notes that the rollout is cohort-gated and can propagate from a top-level session into subagents, so two users on the same version can see different context-loading behavior.

entry.title: [HIGH] Bash allow rules can miss in-project absolute script paths.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.258 macOS VS Code setup found that a project-level permission rule such as `Bash(.claude/scripts/*)` allowed the project-relative script invocation but prompted again when the same script was invoked by its absolute path under the same project root. The PermissionRequest hook then suggested an absolute, machine-specific `Bash(/path/to/project/.claude/scripts/hello *)` rule with a local-settings destination, pushing a team-shareable rule into personal settings drift. Agents and subagents often choose absolute paths when uncertain about the current directory, so a committed allowlist can look correct while still generating prompts or local grants for equivalent in-project commands.

entry.title: [HIGH] Homebrew Bash heredocs can deadlock and truncate target files on macOS.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.260 macOS setup found that Bash-tool heredoc file writes can hang until the 120 second timeout and leave the redirected target as a zero-byte file when PATH resolves `bash` to Homebrew Bash 5.1 or newer. The underlying shell behavior is a Bash heredoc pipe deadlock on macOS's small pipe capacity for bodies above about 512 bytes and below 65536 bytes, but Claude Code amplifies it by using the PATH-selected Bash interpreter and by truncating the target before the heredoc body is successfully delivered. Auto and bypass-permissions modes are especially exposed when their prompt guidance steers routine file writes through `cat <<EOF` instead of the dedicated Write tool.

entry.title: [HIGH] Nested `Agent(type)` allowlists can be ignored in subagent definitions.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.259 macOS repro found that a custom subagent definition with `tools: ["Read", "Agent(inner)"]` could still spawn a sibling subagent type named `other`. The same `Agent(inner)` allowlist was honored when applied to the main thread, and a session-wide `permissions.deny: ["Agent(other)"]` did block the nested spawn, so the denial path reached nested agent calls while the per-subagent allowlist did not. Orchestrator-style agents can therefore appear to have a constrained fan-out surface while still being able to spawn any available subagent type allowed by broader session policy and depth limits.

entry.title: [HIGH] Explicit default `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` can select an empty Keychain store.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.261 macOS setup found that leaving `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` unset and setting it explicitly to the byte-identical default path `$HOME/.claude` can consult different macOS Keychain credential entries. In the repro, ordinary `claude auth status` reported a valid Claude.ai login, while `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR="$HOME/.claude" claude auth status` reported `loggedIn: false` with no diagnostic naming the credential store that had been consulted. Automation that defensively forwards a resolved config directory to child Claude processes can therefore turn a logged-in parent process into an unauthenticated child even though the filesystem path did not actually change.

entry.title: [HIGH] Bash permission dialogs can obscure compound command risk.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code VS Code permission dialog showed dense machine-composed Bash commands in a small monochrome text box, without syntax highlighting, structural line breaks, path emphasis, or a plain-language summary. The user-facing risk is that the final human approval checkpoint can degrade into unreadable raw shell text, especially for compound commands with pipes or `&&`, so users may approve from fatigue rather than actually reviewing what will run.

entry.title: [HIGH] Desktop self-updates can interrupt running sessions.
entry.summary: A reported Windows Claude Desktop 1.46388.3 sideloaded MSIX setup found that the app can stop its own service, replace its package, and restart while a Code session is running. The reporter documented nine registered versions in nine days, including daytime updates and one overnight update that ended roughly seven hours of unattended work. The evidence points to an orchestrated self-update rather than a crash: AppX deployment and CoworkVMService events occur in the same minute, no Crashpad report appears, and the user-facing file-in-use dialog attributes the conflict to another program even though Claude is the program holding the files being replaced. Users running scheduled, remote, or overnight Desktop work therefore cannot treat an alive app window as a stable execution boundary across updates.

entry.title: [CRITICAL] `change_directory` stale project dirs can erase prompts.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Desktop macOS session using Claude Code 2.1.204 found that `change_directory` adopted a new project's settings and hooks while leaving `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` pointed at the scratch workspace where the session launched. A `UserPromptSubmit` hook command that resolved through that stale variable then tried to run a missing script, and CPython returned exit status 2 for ENOENT. Claude Code interpreted that same exit code as an intentional prompt denial, so every later user prompt was blocked and effectively erased while the session could not be asked to diagnose itself.

entry.title: [HIGH] Desktop task sandboxes can clone plugins until disk fills.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Desktop macOS local-agent-mode setup found that `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/local-agent-mode-sessions/<session-id>/<conversation-id>/` accumulated one `local_<uuid>` task sandbox per subagent run and did not remove those directories after tasks completed. Each directory was reported as a full clone of `~/.claude`, dominated by `~/.claude/plugins`, around 300-310 MB per copy. In one active session, roughly 19 task runs created about 8 GB within a few hours, and after manual deletion of more than 100 GB the same session regenerated about 8.8 GB within about an hour of continued subagent-heavy use.

entry.title: [CRITICAL] macOS sandboxed `mktemp` can empty a cleanup target.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.255 macOS sandbox setup found that a template-less `mktemp -d` failed under the Bash tool because BSD `mktemp` chose the Darwin per-user temp directory instead of Claude Code's sandboxed `$TMPDIR`. The failed command substitution left the scratch variable empty, `cd "" && pwd -P` then resolved it to the working directory, and a later bare `rm -rf "$T"` ran against that directory without a recorded critical-path prompt. The reporter saw large local repo damage before the default Bash timeout stopped the tool result, while protected `.git` paths and deny rules limited part of the blast radius.

entry.title: [HIGH] OTLP telemetry can export tool arguments despite `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_*` flags.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.259 macOS setup, also observed on 2.1.252 and 2.1.258, found full Bash command text reaching an OTLP collector even when tool-content-looking flags were unset, set to `0`, or set to `false`. The reporter planted a canary in a Bash command and found it in `tool_decision` `tool_parameters`, `tool_result` `tool_parameters`, and `tool_result` `tool_input`, with `user.email` attached on the same events. The issue is not a model echo path: the canary appeared in tool telemetry attributes, so teams sending Claude Code telemetry directly to a vendor endpoint may export shell commands and user identifiers while believing `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_*` settings suppress tool content.

entry.title: [CRITICAL] Cross-session messaging can bypass folder-scope prompts.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.260 macOS setup found that `ListAgents` and `SendMessage` could move file contents from one live session's working directory into another session without a permission prompt, even though a direct `Read` of the same file across the folder boundary did prompt and was declined. The reporter reproduced both directed and model-selected peer requests in default mode with no user or project settings. In the realistic case, ordinary working notes were relayed by the source session and written into the destination folder, so the effective barrier was the receiving model's content judgement rather than the folder scope the user expected.

entry.title: [CRITICAL] Broad write grants can let the agent edit `.claude/settings.json`.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.260 Windows setup says broad Write/Edit permission grants also allowed the agent to modify `.claude/settings.json`, the project file that defines Claude Code hooks and permissions. That creates a self-modification boundary problem: a session that can rewrite its active policy file may weaken future hook or permission coverage from inside the same project. Older reports and some modes showed `.claude/` self-modification being blocked, so this should be treated as path- and version-sensitive until reproduced on the exact client, IDE, permission mode, and settings scope in use.

entry.title: [CRITICAL] Plan Mode can show active while Write runs without an approved plan.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.260 Windows CLI session using a custom Anthropic-compatible endpoint showed Plan Mode active through both `/plan` and Shift+Tab, while a direct `Write` tool call still ran before any accepted plan, permission prompt, `EnterPlanMode`, or `ExitPlanMode` transition. The reporter verified the target file changed outside Claude Code with PowerShell. An older 2.1.65 observation under `permissions.defaultMode: "plan"` also showed `No plan found` before execution continued, but that transcript is no longer available. The official Anthropic endpoint is not yet confirmed, so the root cause may be client enforcement, endpoint compatibility, or an interaction between them. The user-facing risk is still concrete: Plan Mode UI state and injected instructions are not enough proof that mutating tools are blocked in that launch path.

entry.title: [HIGH] Auto mode denials can compound and block approved repair steps.
entry.summary: Reported Claude Code auto-mode sessions show the classifier blocking later actions after an earlier denial in the same conversation, even when the later action was explicitly authorized by the user or was read-only inspection. One Linux aarch64 report describes an initially denied read-only production SQLite query over SSH, followed later by denial of the project's own deploy script after tests and backup, denial of the user's request to add a narrow Bash allow rule, and denial of reading `~/.claude/settings.json` to inspect the active permissions. A separate macOS report saw `gh pr merge` denied after an explicit merge instruction, then a read-only `gh search issues` command denied with the same generic classifier reason. The result is a recovery trap: the classifier blocks the operation, the suggested permission-rule repair, and sometimes the evidence-gathering step needed to diagnose it.

entry.title: [HIGH] Read deny rules can force manual Bash search prompts for recursive searches.
entry.summary: Reported Claude Code 2.1.257 through 2.1.260-era regressions show that when a `Read(...)` deny rule is configured, ordinary Bash search commands can trigger a manual approval prompt even when the searched files do not match the denied pattern. Repros include `cd DIR && grep ... relative/path`, `grep -r` or `rg` with include filters that exclude `.env`, and background subagents running in `bypassPermissions` or auto mode. One report traced the arming condition to the existence of any `Read(...)` deny rule, so server-managed secret rules for `.env`, `*.pem`, or `id_rsa` could gate unrelated relative test-file reads that could not match those patterns. A later 2.1.260 report narrowed one live trigger to leading-`./` root-file rules: `Read(./.env)` made `grep -rl pattern .` prompt, while `Read(.env)` still denied direct `.env` reads but let the root recursive search run. The prompt is described as bypass-immune and classifier-unroutable in public confirmations, so unattended agents can stall waiting for a human even though the command is read-only and the session was configured to avoid prompts.
